memory_versions.text:
Order intake notes:

- Form version 1 requires all six canonical fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize source aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - prio → priority
- Do not omit priority or ship_country, even when intake notes say “ordinary priority” or duplicate checks are complete.
- Validate every field before submission. Missing/invalid priority and ship_country caused repeated rejections; missing qty also caused rejection.
- A retry can succeed after correcting invalid fields (ORD-5101, ORD-5103, ORD-5108), so preserve valid values and repair only flagged fields.
- Three failed attempts exhaust the record and send it to manual review (ORD-5104–5106). Avoid spending the final attempt without checking every required field.
- Customer confirmation requests imply the provided email should be retained accurately; do not alter email values.

Order intake notes:

- Form versions 1 and 2 require all six canonical fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - prio → priority
- “Ordinary priority,” duplicate-check completion, partner-portal origin, or confirmation-email requests do not supply valid priority or ship_country. Enter explicit valid values; never infer or omit them.
- Validate every field before submission, especially priority, ship_country, and qty. Recent batches repeatedly failed because priority/ship_country were invalid or missing; ORD-5110/5111 also had invalid qty.
- Preserve valid values and repair only flagged fields when retrying. A corrected retry can succeed (ORD-5101, ORD-5103, ORD-5108), but do not retry while any required field remains unchecked.
- Three failed attempts exhaust the record and send it to manual review (ORD-5104–5106, ORD-5110–5117). Treat attempt 2 or 3 as high risk: perform a complete validation before submitting.
- Customer confirmation requests imply the supplied email must be retained exactly; never alter it.
- Source records may be truncated or malformed in the intake display. Do not submit until all six values are actually present and valid; escalate for missing source data rather than guessing.

Order intake notes:

- Form versions 1–3 require exactly six canonical fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - prio → priority
- Validate every field before submission, including date format/validity, priority, qty, and ship_country. Recent failures show order_date can be rejected even when it appears populated; do not assume a displayed date is acceptable.
- Priority must be an explicit valid value. “Ordinary priority,” priority levels such as 0, duplicate-check completion, partner-portal origin, and confirmation requests do not provide priority or ship_country. Never infer, omit, or substitute them.
- Source records may be truncated, malformed, handwritten, or contain stray fields (status, reason, errors). Use only six verified canonical values; escalate when any required value is missing, ambiguous, or invalid rather than guessing.
- Preserve valid values and repair only confirmed/flagged fields on retry. Do not retry until all six fields have been fully revalidated. Validate the entire record especially on attempts 2–3.
- Three failed attempts exhaust the record and send it to manual review. Recent batches confirm repeated invalid fields across all attempts and explicit escalation when no valid priority is available.
- Customer confirmation requests imply the supplied email must be retained exactly; never alter it.
- Alias normalization does not repair missing data: a truncated “quantity” or “prio” value remains unusable until its complete valid value is available.

Order intake notes:

- Form versions 1–4 require exactly six canonical fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize only confirmed aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - prio → priority
  Do not accept unsupported aliases such as priority_level or stray/source keys.
- Submit only the six canonical fields. Exclude status, reason, errors, metadata, and any unrecognized fields; these can cause rejection.
- Validate all six fields before every submission, especially order_date (must be a valid accepted date, not merely populated), priority, qty, and ship_country. Null, truncated, malformed, ambiguous, or missing values remain invalid.
- Priority must be explicitly supplied as a valid value. Do not infer it from “ordinary priority,” numeric levels such as 0, duplicate-check completion, partner-portal origin, or other notes. These notes also do not supply ship_country.
- Alias normalization cannot repair incomplete data. Escalate rather than guess when any required value is unavailable.
- Preserve valid values and repair only confirmed/flagged fields on retry, but revalidate the entire six-field record before each attempt, particularly attempts 2–3.
- Customer confirmation requests imply the supplied email must be retained exactly; never modify it.
- Do not include confirmation requests, provenance, or handwritten/transcription context as field values.
- Three failed attempts exhaust the record and require manual review. Repeated failures commonly involve missing/invalid order_date, priority, qty, or ship_country; manual-review payloads and their explanatory fields must not be submitted as order fields.

Order intake notes:

- Form versions 1–5 require exactly six canonical fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Confirmed aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - prio → priority
  - contact_email → email
- Normalize aliases before submission and submit only the six canonical fields. Never submit both an alias and its canonical field; duplicate email representations can cause rejection.
- Do not accept unsupported aliases such as priority_level or stray/source keys. Exclude status, reason, errors, metadata, provenance, confirmation requests, and transcription context.
- Validate every field before every attempt. A populated ISO-looking date may still be invalid: verify it meets the accepted date/range rules. Also validate priority, qty, and ship_country; missing, malformed, ambiguous, truncated, or null values remain invalid.
- Priority must be explicitly supplied and valid. Never infer it from “ordinary priority,” numeric levels, portal origin, duplicate-check completion, or notes. Notes likewise do not supply ship_country.
- Preserve confirmed values, especially email (retain the supplied address exactly). Repair only confirmed or flagged fields, then revalidate the entire six-field record before retrying.
- Alias normalization cannot repair incomplete data. Escalate rather than guess.
- Three failed attempts exhaust the record and require manual review. Repeated failures commonly involve order_date, priority, qty, or ship_country. Manual-review payloads and explanations must not be submitted as order fields.

Order intake notes:

- Versions 1–6 require exactly six canonical fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Normalize confirmed aliases before submission:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - contact_email → email
  - prio → priority
- Version 6 displays contact_email and units, but submit only canonical names. Never submit contact_email, units, or both an alias and canonical field. “Units” is not a confirmed alias for qty; obtain/confirm the quantity mapping rather than guessing.
- Reject unsupported aliases such as priority_level or shipping_country, and exclude stray/source keys.
- Submit no status, reason, errors, metadata, provenance, manual_review payload, confirmation request, portal/front-desk context, or transcription context as order fields.
- Validate all six fields before every attempt. Dates must satisfy accepted format and range rules; also validate priority, qty, and ship_country. Missing, malformed, ambiguous, truncated, or null values are invalid.
- Priority must be explicitly supplied and valid. Never infer it from “ordinary priority,” numeric levels, portal origin, duplicate-check completion, or notes. Notes do not supply ship_country.
- Preserve confirmed values, especially the supplied email exactly. Repair only confirmed or explicitly flagged fields, then revalidate the complete record.
- Alias normalization cannot repair incomplete data. Escalate rather than guess.
- Three failed attempts exhaust the record and require manual review. Do not submit the manual-review explanation or payload as order data. Recent failures reinforce that missing priority/ship_country, unsupported aliases, malformed dates, and incomplete qty commonly cause rejection.

Order intake notes:

- Submit exactly six canonical fields: cust, email, order_date, priority, qty, ship_country.
- Version 7 displays contact_email, cust, placed_on, priority, ship_country, units. Display labels are not submission names:
  - contact_email → email only when the value is confirmed
  - placed_on is not yet a confirmed alias for order_date; confirm mapping before use
  - units is not a confirmed alias for qty; never guess
- Normalize only confirmed aliases:
  - customer → cust
  - quantity → qty
  - contact_email → email
  - prio → priority
- Never submit display aliases (contact_email, placed_on, units), unsupported aliases (priority_level, shipping_country), duplicate alias/canonical fields, or stray/source keys.
- Exclude status, reason, errors, metadata, provenance, manual-review data, confirmation requests, and front-desk, portal, duplicate-check, or transcription context.
- Validate all six canonical fields before every attempt. Missing, malformed, ambiguous, truncated, null, or incomplete values are invalid. Apply date format/range checks and validate priority, qty, and ship_country.
- Priority must be explicitly supplied and valid. Do not infer it from “ordinary priority,” numeric levels, portal origin, duplicate-check completion, or notes. Notes do not supply ship_country.
- Preserve confirmed values, especially email, exactly. Repair only confirmed or explicitly flagged fields, then revalidate the complete record.
- Alias normalization cannot repair incomplete records. Escalate rather than guess.
- Three failed attempts exhaust the record and require manual review; never submit the explanation or payload as order data. Recent version-7 failures reinforce that contact_email, units, missing ship_country, malformed/truncated source data, and incomplete qty commonly cause rejection.
